#1296. Longest Unbeaten Runs in International Football History

Going unbeaten in international football, where every side is measured by the FIFA World Ranking, is harder than it may first appear. In club football, managers and head coaches see their players almost every day, and so have the opportunity to embed their tactics and style of play into their players. National team managers, however, can go months between international breaks without overseeing a single game or training session. That's what makes a long run without defeat one of the sport's rarest achievements.

The longest runs belong to some of the greatest sides the game has seen. Several of them have won major tournaments along the way, and one turned a World Cup final into a record-breaking night. Some ended in famous upsets, and some came to a stop in games few people remember.

Here's a look at the top five longest unbeaten runs in men's international football history.

GIVEMESPORT takes a look at the greatest footballers to ever play at the World Cup.

Spain's golden generation started their 35-game unbeaten streak in February 2007, when Andrés Iniesta, one of the greatest midfielders in history, scored his first goal for the Spanish national team during a 1-0 win over England at Old Trafford. In a run initially started by head coach Luis Aragonés, La Roja entered the 2008 European Championship having failed to win only twice in their previous 16 games, with draws against Iceland and Finland.

After topping their group, Spain needed penalties to edge past Italy in the quarter-finals, before dismantling Russia 3-0 in the semis. Fernando Torres' 33rd minute strike made the difference in the final against Germany as the Spanish won their first major trophy in 44 years and their second Euros title. With the likes of Carles Puyol, Xavi and David Villa at his disposal, new boss Vicente del Bosque maintained the run after taking over the national team following the tournament. Eventually, it was the USA who put an end to Spain's unbeaten run, with a 2-0 victory in the 2009 Confederations Cup semi-final, with goals from Jozy Altidore and Clint Dempsey.

Brazil share the fourth longest unbeaten run, having also lasted 35 games without defeat between 1993 and 1996. Rivaldo scored the only goal in a friendly against Mexico in December 1993 to start the run under coach Carlos Alberto Parreira. The Brazil national team entered the 1994 World Cup in the USA in good form, having not lost any of their last six games, including an 8-2 thrashing of Honduras just two weeks before the tournament.

Despite drawing their final group stage game against Sweden, Canarinho topped their group and dumped the host nation from the tournament in the Round of 16. Victories over the Netherlands and Sweden in the knockouts set Brazil up for a World Cup final against Italy. With the teams stuck at 0-0 after extra time, the game was decided by penalties, with Italy's Roberto Baggio missing the decisive spot kick to gift the title to the South-American nation.

Mario Zagallo took over the reins as coach of the national team, and carried the unbeaten streak through the 1995 Copa América. Although his side did lose the final to hosts Uruguay, that was only through penalties, meaning they were still unbeaten after extra time. Ironically, the nation whom the run started against also ended the run, with Mexico winning the Gold Cup final 2-0 in January 1996.

A look at some of the most impressive runs without losing in the Premier League

The first game of Argentina's 36-game unbeaten run would likely have been one that they didn't want to play. Having lost 2-0 to Brazil in the 2019 Copa América semi-finals, Argentina faced Chile for the third-place trophy, in what many view as a glorified friendly. However, it was only up from here, as they beat Chile 2-1 and started their unbeaten run.

Three years later, the run was still going strong as Argentina started their 2021 Copa América campaign. After topping their five-team group, Argentina dumped Ecuador and Colombia from the competition to set up a rematch of their 2019 semi-final against Brazil. Ángel Di María's first-half strike was enough to secure their first title in 28 years, and Lionel Messi, one of the greatest football players of all time, lifted his first senior international trophy.

Argentina's special run lasted right up until the first fixture of the next major tournament, having beaten Italy 3-0 in the 2022 Finalissima at Wembley, before falling to a shock 2-1 defeat to Saudi Arabia in their first game of the 2022 FIFA World Cup. And whilst the end of such an impressive run would've been disappointing, the Argentina national side turned it around and won the tournament.

Found an error? Send it info@www.givemesport.com so it can be corrected.

Having failed to qualify for the 2018 World Cup, a 1-0 defeat to Portugal in September 2018 seemed an unlikely place for the Italian national team to turn their fortunes around, with the former European giants seemingly at rock bottom. And whilst their 1-1 draw with Ukraine that October didn't seem to be much of an improvement, it kickstarted what would be the second-longest unbeaten run in men's international football history.

Roberto Mancini managed to harness the experience of the likes of Giorgio Chiellini and Leonardo Bonucci ahead of the Euro 2020 competition and got the Italian national team in good form. After topping their group, they defeated Austria, Belgium and Spain on their way to a Wembley final against England, which they won on penalties.

Eventually, the run came to an end, with a 2-1 defeat to Spain in the Nations League semi-final in October 2021, in what was the Azzurri's first competitive home defeat since 1999.

Just days after a 1-0 friendly loss against Colombia, Spain's record-breaking run began with a 3-3 draw against Brazil in March 2024. That summer, Luis de la Fuente's side put in a special performance at the 2024 European Championship. The Spanish national team won all seven of their games, including 2–1 wins over Germany and France on their way to a final against England, which they also won 2-1.

Similar results followed in the 2025 Nations League, as the Spaniards reached the final, and faced Portugal. Whilst they did lose that final, it was via penalties. Therefore, they were still unbeaten after extra time. Their 2026 World Cup campaign started disappointingly, with a goalless draw against Cape Verde. They then beat the likes of Portugal, Belgium and France on their way to what would be a record-breaking World Cup final against Argentina.

With the match goalless after 90 minutes, it was substitute Ferran Torres who broke the deadlock in the 104th minute. Spain managed to hold on, won their second World Cup, and broke Italy's record to make it 38-games unbeaten.

Spain continued their unbeaten run after the World Cup, but it came to a juddering halt in November 2026 when England defeated them 3-2 in Madrid. The Spanish media described the loss to Thomas Tuchel's men as "the biggest set-back of the De La Fuente era", noting that England were "steely and composed" victors.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

#1294. Newspapers deliver mixed verdicts after Italy’s Nations League collapse against Belgium

Newspapers in Italy have delivered mixed verdicts following the national team’s 4-1 defeat against Belgium on Sunday evening, which saw the Azzurri knocked out of the Nations League despite starting the evening at the top of the group.

Italy had started Sunday in first place in their Nations League group following an impressive 3-1 win at home against France on Thursday night, but ended up in third place after losing 4-1 to Belgium and seeing France claim a 2-1 victory over Turkey.

The in-form Pio Esposito opened the scoring with his 10th goal for the Nazionale, but Italy would go on to concede three goals within 11 minutes from Maxim De Cuyper, Nathan Ngoy and Jeremy Doku in the first half. Milan’s Diego Moreira added a fourth towards the end and Esposito missed a penalty to make the scores 4-2.

The reactions in the Italian press on Monday morning have brought mixed reviews.

La Gazzetta dello Sport criticised Mancini’s decisions on the night, particularly his personnel choices with an untested front three of Esposito, Luca Koleosho and out-of-position central midfielder Niccolo Pisilli starting across the front three together for the first time.

The Pink Paper felt that Italy had a strong opening 10 minutes, resulting in Esposito’s 10th Azzurri goal, but that they simply stopped playing from that point onwards. They suggest that on another night, Italy could have conceded twice as many goals as they did.

However, La Gazzetta dello Sport admits that it is better for this sort of result and performance to have happened now rather than later down the line.

The Corriere dello Sport agreed that Italy could have conceded several more had it not been for a solid performance between the sticks from Gianluigi Donnarumma and that Italy’s first-half collapse was a major disappointment after all the hard work they had put in in their previous Nations League outings.

Pisilli and Nicolo Fagioli were singled out for individual criticism after being hooked at half-time, but there was praise for Esposito, who is now up to 10 goals from his first 15 national team caps.

The Corriere dello Sport concludes that ‘you can’t ask youngsters to learn and grow and then demolish them for their mistakes, we must support them’.

Tuttosport agrees that there have still been plenty of positives from Italy’s Nations League campaign and insists that the Azzurri have ‘come a long way’ since their first game against Belgium back in September.

Tuttosport pointed out that Italy did well to pick up 10 points from a group that contained France, Belgium and Turkey, who all went to the 2026 World Cup that the Azzurri infamously missed out on.

They praised Mancini for bringing Italy back to modern European standards by deploying a 4-3-3 and praised his confidence in young players and his ability to get the best out of Esposito at centre-forward.

The major issue that Tuttosport pointed to was with Italy’s defence, given that they failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their six Nations League group stage fixtures, even conceding twice against Turkey, who finished the group stage with six straight defeats.

Still, Tuttosport urges Italy to look to the future and to focus on the upcoming Euro 2028 qualifiers, which are more important than the Nations League campaign anyway.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1293. The England National Football Team's Best Away Wins of All Time

Winning on the road is one of the best feelings in football, and it's even harder at international level. Hostile crowds, unfamiliar conditions and some of the finest sides on the planet have tripped up generation after generation of brilliant Three Lions squads.

Every so often, though, England produce a night that makes it into the history books. Thomas Tuchel's side added to that list on November 15, 2026, when ten men held on to beat world champions Spain 3-2 in Madrid.

That result ended a 43-game unbeaten run and sent England into the Nations League knockout stages as group winners. But where does it sit among the greatest away wins in the nation's history?

Bobby Robson's England arrived in Rio de Janeiro under pressure after being booed off at Wembley following a 2-0 defeat to the USSR days earlier. What followed was one of the most famous goals ever scored in an England shirt.

A 20-year-old John Barnes chested down Mark Hateley's pass on the left, cut inside and glided past a string of yellow shirts before slotting home just before the break. He then turned provider, crossing for Hateley to head in for the second.

It was England's first win over Brazil in 28 years, and their first ever at the Maracanã and remains a historic victory.

Roy Hodgson's side were not considered among the best in the world at this time after a difficult period for the national team, and they certainly looked beaten when Mario Gomez headed reigning world champions Germany two goals clear just before the hour, after Toni Kroos had opened the scoring late in the first half.

Instead, England produced a stunning fightback. Harry Kane dragged them back into it with a Cruyff turn and a precise finish inside the far post. Substitute Jamie Vardy then levelled with a brilliant improvised flick at the near post, before Dier rose to head Jordan Henderson's corner home in stoppage time.

It was Eric Dier's first international goal, and the start of a Euro 2016 build-up that promised far more than it delivered.

A month after losing 2-1 to Spain at Wembley, Gareth Southgate's World Cup semi-finalists travelled to Seville and blew Luis Enrique's side away with a fantastic counter-attacking performance. England were 3-0 up by half-time.

Raheem Sterling ended a three-year wait for an England goal with a double, Marcus Rashford added the other, and Kane had a hand in all three. Paco Alcácer and Sergio Ramos made the finish nervy, but England held firm.

The result inflicted Spain's first competitive home defeat since 2003, marked the first time they had ever conceded three in a competitive home match, and gave England their first win on Spanish soil since 1987.

It also gave fans an all-time great cult moment, as Dier was carded for what seemed to be a compeltely fair, albeit aggressive, tackle on Ramos in which he received a yellow card, but also earned the respect of an entire nation.

Spain entered as the reigning world and European champions, unbeaten in 43 matches and having already beaten England 3-2 at Wembley in recent months. Then, for an hour, England made them look ordinary.

Tuchel's side pressed relentlessly, and Kane converted a penalty on the stroke of halftime after being fouled by the 2026 Golden Boy winner, Pau Cubarsí. Tempers also flared at half-time, as there was no love lost between two of the elite international sides.

Ezri Konsa powered in a header from Declan Rice's corner after the break, and Ben White finished through Unai Simón's legs four minutes later. Things couldn't have been going better, until Elliot Anderson's red card for a foul on Lamine Yamal ensured the game flipped on its head.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored the resulting penalty and Nico Williams added a second, but James Trafford's stoppage-time double save sealed a record tenth straight away win. It was also England's first victory in Madrid since Gary Lineker scored all four in a 4-2 win at the Bernabéu in 1987.

The Spanish teenager's comments have resurfaced after England beat Spain and Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or.

This is still the one to beat, even 25 years later. Germany had led the qualifying group and had lost just once at home in qualifiers when Sven-Göran Eriksson's England arrived in Munich. Carsten Jancker's sixth-minute opener suggested business as usual as England faced an uphill task.

What followed remains the gold standard. Michael Owen equalised, Steven Gerrard fired home his first England goal from distance before half-time, and Owen struck twice more after the break to become the first Englishman since Geoff Hurst in 1966 to score a hat-trick against Germany. Finally, Emile Heskey completed the rout.

England went on to top the group, and Owen won the Ballon d'Or months later and that night in Munich remains the most special away day for the Three Lions to date.

The Three Lions have made plenty of friends and foes during their international travels...

AWAY DAYS: Which England away win was most memorable for you? Share your thoughts in the comments.

#1292. Goalkeeper scores one of the most bizarre own goals EVER during play-off clash in Argentina

Published: 14:49 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:54 EST, 15 November 2026

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

As he tried to throw the ball out, though, he got it all wrong and ended up launching the ball into his own net.

Bacher, 30, essentially failed to let go of the ball at the right time, leaving his team-mates stunned.

The player himself covered his face with his hand before retrieving the ball to get play started again.

Arsenal players wheeled off in celebration, only for Comunicaciones to level things up in the game soon after. Arsenal, though, scored again, and eventually won 3-2 in the first leg of the tie.

"Están matando al fútbol"Por el "insólito" gol en contra que se hace el arquero de Comunicaciones ante Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/GLUJlcKPXK

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored a bizarre own goal during his side's third-tier play-off game

Bacher joined the club at the start of last year, but has always played in his homeland of Argentina.

#1291. Newspaper names six players Italy should build around for 2030 World Cup

Despite a 4-1 hammering away against Belgium on Sunday evening, Italy have been urged to look for the positives after a largely positive Nations League campaign and La Gazzetta dello Sport has named six players that Roberto Mancini should build around in the years approaching the 2030 World Cup.

Italy were defeated 4-1 in Brussels by Belgium on Sunday night despite opening the scoring after 10 minutes through Pio Esposito. Maxim De Cuyper, Nathan Ngoy and Jeremy Doku scored three goals within 11 minutes in the first half and Milan’s Diego Moreira added a fourth 10 minutes before time.

Despite starting the night at the top of their group, the 4-1 defeat saw both Belgium and France overtake Italy, who finished the group in third place and will not be progressing to the Nations League quarter-finals.

Still, many pundits and analysts have urged Italy to look for the positives after picking up 10 points from their last five matches in a tough group that also contained France and Turkey.

La Gazzetta dello Sport suggests that Italy’s mix of emerging youngsters and experienced core players will stand them in good stead heading into the next few major tournaments.

The Pink Paper wrote that everybody knew that Gianluigi Donnarumma was a top-quality player well before the latest set of Nations League fixtures, but that it is encouraging to now be able to include Pio Esposito in the same category at the other end of the pitch.

La Gazzetta dello Sport suggests that these are the two players that Italy must build their future and upcoming qualification campaigns around, along with the core of Nicolo Barella, Sandro Tonali and Alessandro Bastoni. Michael Kayode also appears a lock-in at right-back for the foreseeable future.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1289. Striker Che Adams says Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli is big on the small details... 'he loves his FaceTime calls'

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be big on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the new man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli

Striker Adams says Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’

Hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’

John McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

‘He said to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very important to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ said Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’

#1288. Three winners and three losers of Mancini’s new crop of Italy internationals

Italy’s Nations League journey has come to a premature end after Sunday’s 4-1 defeat away against Belgium, and though the campaign finished in disappointment, the last few weeks have brought opportunities for a number of new, young faces in the Nazionale squad: Here are three who impressed when given the opportunity and three who still have room for improvement.

Italy were defeated 4-1 by Belgium in Brussels on Sunday evening, despite a 10th-minute opener from Inter’s Pio Esposito. Three goals within 11 minutes from Maxim De Cuyper Nathan Ngoy and Jeremy Doku shifted the balance of the game and a late fourth from Diego Moreira put the game beyond any doubt.

Despite starting the night at the top of the group, Sunday’s defeat against Belgium saw Italy overtaken both by their opponents and by France, who claimed a 2-1 victory over Turkey in their final group stage fixture.

Still, many outlets have urged Italy to look for the positive in spite of Sunday’s defeat against Belgium. Roberto Mancini and his players had picked up 10 points from their last five matches in a tough group and showed plenty of promise and character after a miserable year that had seen them miss out on qualification to the 2026 World Cup.

Though Mancini did not get his selections right against Belgium, he has largely been praised for his willingness to put faith in youth: Only three of Italy’s starters on Sunday were born before the year 2000 and five of them were aged 22 or below.

Mancini also gave opportunities to several players who had previously been overlooked, including Brentford right-back Michael Kayode, who now looks a nailed-on first-choice on the right of Italy’s back four for the foreseeable future. Of all the new faces that Mancini has introduced over the last few weeks, his emergence has arguably been the most encouraging.

Sporting CP midfielder Issa Doumbia has also earned praise in the Italian press on Monday: TMW credited his physical qualities but admitted that he still has room for improvement in terms of game management, but assessed his performances as generally positive when given the opportunity.

Napoli’s Antonio Vergara was also impressive on Italy’s right flank during this international break and has handled the step up to international football comfortably. TMW argues that he should be the go-to starter in that position for the time being.

There are, however, a few of the new Italy faces that may still need a bit more time, including two of the front three that started against Belgium on Sunday night. This was perhaps a touch too soon for Luca Koleosho, who remains untested at the highest levels, while Niccolo Pisilli also struggled to impress, albeit out of position on the right wing instead of his usual position in central midfield.

Sebastiano Esposito, who was dropped from the Italy squad on Sunday, will also be hoping for a touch more consistency in his performances, despite some encouraging moments during this Nations League campaign.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1287. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

#1286. ‘Tactical genius’ Emery outsmarts Maresca as City crash to first league defeat

Enzo Maresca’s flawless start to the Premier League with Manchester City is over after another masterclass from Unai Emery.

Matches at Villa Park were a notoriously chastening experience for Pep Guardiola and it was the same old story for Maresca as City have now lost on their last four visits here.

On his fourth anniversary in charge of Villa, there was more tactical brilliance from Emery, who also did the double over Guardiola last season. It was Emery’s £65m record signing Nicolas Jackson who again underlined how some managers can get the best out of certain players.

Jackson had been a target for Emery ever since the Basque’s appointment and now has seven goals in claret and blue. It will have been an especially sweet moment for the Senegal forward, for it was Maresca who allowed him to join Bayern Munich on loan while he was in charge at Chelsea.

City’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Guéhi endured a particularly difficult afternoon and was at fault for Jackson’s stunning first goal. The centre-back has struggled in recent weeks with a bad mistake in England’s defeat by Spain and he was exposed for both Ipswich goals last week. He was replaced at half-time after a booking for a foul on the excellent Jackson.

“Saturday will mark four years since Villa unveiled Emery as their head coach and few could have predicted the success that has followed. He has proved an inspired appointment who has continually embarrassed the “Big Six” clubs.

“On every level, he has delivered: points per game, net spend, a distinguishable style of play, improving individual players, over-performance in the league and European competition.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

Of course, City’s campaign remains overshadowed by the recent guilty verdict from the Premier League over financial regulations.

#1285. Pagliuca analyses Belgium’s ‘deserved’ victory over Italy and advises Donnarumma

Former Italy goalkeeper Gianluca Pagliuca has delivered his verdict after Sunday’s 4-1 Nations League defeat against Belgium, feels that it is only natural that the Azzurri encounter a few difficulties during a rebuild phase and has explained where Gianluigi Donnarumma went wrong with his error against France on Thursday night.

Italy’s Nations League campaign came to a premature end after a 4-1 defeat away against Belgium in Brussels on Sunday evening. The Azzurri had started the night in first place in their group, but were overtaken by both their opponents on the night and by France, whom they had beaten 3-1 earlier in the week.

Italy had started brightly against Belgium, taking the lead through the in-form Pio Esposito within the first 11 minutes of the game.

Pagliuca, speaking to Radio Anch’io Sport on Monday morning, said that he thought that Italy were going to pick up where they had left off against France.

“At first I thought it was going to be a continuation of the performance from the France game, but then Belgium’s comeback began,” said the former Azzurri goalkeeper. “We suffered a lot in the second half as well. Belgium deserved it, they are more ready than us at the moment.”

Pagliuca feels that it is only normal that Italy aren’t quite up to the level just yet at this stage of Mancini’s rebuild: “I think it’s normal for a national team that is still being rebuilt to not have players at the same level of a team like France.”

He feels that Italy struggled defensively against Belgium, but, again, that this is only normal.

“We suffered against Belgium’s fast attackers. Calafiori and Bastoni, who were perfect against France, suffered yesterday as well. However, I don’t think there’s a big defensive problem. The game is a lot quicker now and more planned in attack, which means you are going to suffer a bit more defensively, but that is the same for everyone.”

Mancini’s inclusion of several youngsters over the last few weeks has gone down positively among supporters and pundits. Only three players of Italy’s starting XI on Sunday night were born before the year 2000 and five of them were aged 22 or under.

“There are lots of good young players, there’s not just one in particular,” said Pagliuca. “I think the coach, who wants to aim for the EUROs and World Cup, needs a period to test a few things out. I think it’s right to call up players even if they are not starters at club level.

“Mancini is experimenting. He will also call up some of the more experienced players for the qualifying matches. For now, he wants to test young players and see what they’re made of. The Nations League does have value, but the important thing is to qualify for the EUROs and World Cup.”

Pagliuca was asked for his thoughts on Donnarumma’s recent performances and the error that he made that led to France’s only goal in Thursday’s 3-1 win in San Siro.

“Sometimes, goalkeepers want to overdo it,” he explained. “Gigio made a mistake against France on Thursday because he was overdoing it. A goalkeeper has to do the simple things correctly. But, he made up for it by making great saves, yesterday as well.”

Lastly, on Pio Esposito, Pagliuca added: “He has also played a lot of games and is improving with every appearance. He’s cool in front of goal and is having a great season.

“I think Cristian Chivu will stick to playing with two strikers for now, but maybe we’ll start to see all three of them at some point in most games. Inter are the clear favourites for the Scudetto and I think they will win the league.”

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1284. Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admits his newlook team need to deliver sooner rather than later

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.

Appointed Steve Clarke’s successor in the summer, the Belgian’s attempts to bring in fresh faces and a new style of play has produced mixed results in his opening five Nations League games.

Following Friday’s win over North Macedonia, John McGinn warned the Tartan Army that it could take as long as 18 months for everything to click into place.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

Asked if he felt he had to deliver sooner, he said: ‘Yeah, for sure, but we’re only talking about 18 months because John said that. He could have said 15 months. I don’t know. But, for sure, it needs to be quicker.

‘In 18 months, it will be the time of the Euros and that is what he meant. We have to go there and be prepared for this in 18 months’ time.

Sebastien Pocognoli  says his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'

‘For sure, game after game, we need to see improvement.

‘Some new faces will come back in March. So, step by step we will have more ideas and in one month’s time a lot can change also.’

McGinn also said that the players were fully behind the manager, reiterating the point previously made by Andy Robertson and Scott McTominay.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most important part.

‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager said: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’

Pocognoli’s side were booed off at half-time on Friday with criticism of the performance persisting despite them going on to win the game.

But the manager claims he’s oblivious to wider concerns about the performances to date, saying: ‘No, I’m not aware of this. That’s why I was surprised (at the question).

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli

‘Yes, there were some boos at half-time. I think that’s part of it, it’s been like this for years.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

‘But there there were also a lot of positives after the North Macedonia game.

‘I was the first one to say calm down as we need to see more.’

#1283. How Belgium defeat changes Italy’s qualifying campaign for EURO 2028

Italy were knocked out of the Nations League at the end of the group stage following a 4-1 defeat away against Belgium in Brussels on Sunday night, which means that Roberto Mancini and his players will be involved in EURO 2028 qualifiers instead of the Nations League quarter-finals during the next international break.

Sunday’s defeat against Belgium was Italy’s final international fixture of the calendar year, and when they return to action in March, the focus will have already turned to qualification for the next major tournament: EURO 2028.

The 4-1 loss against Belgium saw Italy finish their Nations League group in third place, despite starting the night in first, and means that Italy will not be taking part in the Nations League quarter-finals in March. They will kick off their EURO qualifying campaign instead.

The nations involved in qualification for EURO 2028 will be divided into 12 groups of either four or five. As Italy have not qualified for the Nations League quarter-finals, they will be placed into a group of five rather than four and will begin their qualification campaign in March, rather than September.

Italy will face the other four teams in their qualifying group home and away. Nations that finish at the top of their group will qualify directly for the final tournament, as will the eight best-ranked runners up.

The four remaining runners up, along with the best-ranked non-qualified group winners from the Nations League will compete in the play-offs.

The EURO 2028 qualifying draw will take place in Belfast on Sunday, December 6 at 17.00 GMT.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1281. Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa

From the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”

Some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Konsa, 29, has quickly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

The victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his new surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

“Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

They kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

Probably sums up Zubimendi’s season so far that he finally gets some meaningful minutes in the Premier League and ends up getting smashed in the face and covered in his own blood. This is after he got injured in a cool-down a few weeks ago. When your luck’s out...

Brilliant play from Oscar Bobb as he cuts inside on his left foot and bends a shot into the far bottom corner for the away side.

Treatment is needed for Zubimendi after he is caught on the nose by Barry.

Big chance for Everton. Garner whips a teasing cross into the box, Dewsbury-Hall meets it with his head on the run but the ball flies just wide of the post.

EvertonOFF Johnson, Mykolenko ON Dibling, Hackney

Tarkowski is the latest yellow card for Everton after a foul on Havertz.

Eze with a poor cross into the box. He fails to run back quickly and Arteta sprints to the edge of the touchline and goes berserk at the midfielder.

How have Arsenal reacted to their top scorer Saka being injured? Both of their centre backs have scored for the first time this season.

On his 200 Premier League appearance for Arsenal, Gabriel marks it with his first goal of the season.

It is a lovely move with slick one-touch passing. The ball is fed to White making a run down the outside and he clips the ball to the far post for Gabriel to head home.

OFF Merino, Lewis-Skelly, GyokeresON Calafiori, Guimaraes, Havertz

Garner is booked for Everton now after barging into Merino off the ball.

Arteta is shown a yellow card for something. Not sure what for yet. But the Arsenal manager is looking to make some changes off the bench.

Arsenal have been guilty of overplaying today. Opting for the extra pass rather than taking a shot. The game is open at the moment and that makes things dangerous for the home side.

Yellow card for Lewis-Skelly after bringing down Johnson. Gabriel is back on the pitch and seems happy enough to continue.

Arsenal have defensive options in Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori and Mosquera if Arteta wants to avoid taking any risks.

A worry for Arsenal as Gabriel jars his knee into the ground as he tries to clear the ball. The Brazilian is receiving treatment and hobbles off the pitch.

Gabriel immediately raised his hand for medical attention after making that clearance. He really extended his leg to get the ball away. Looks to be in a lot of pain.

Latest corner from Arsenal after Eze’s shot is blocked by Rohl. Rice’s delivery into the near post is headed clear to Odegaard, who shoots ambitiously from distance and Pickford collects the ball comfortably.

Arsenal get the match restarted. The longer the match goes on without extending the lead, Everton will think they have a chance.

Before today, Arsenal had averaged five corners per match in the Premier League this season. In the first 45 minutes here, they had 10 corners.

Yellow card for Mykolenko after he catches White wide on the right. Rice whips the ball in and Merino meets it with a flick goalwards but the ball goes over the bar.

That is the final touch of the half and the players are running off to get dry!

Big chance for Everton. White thinks he has time when he heads the ball back to Raya but he does not connect well and Barry is there to pick it up and he flicks a shot at goal but Raya reacts quickly to parry the ball.

Raya is penalised for taking too long with the ball and Everton have a cheap corner. Danger is cleared by Arsenal as they force Everton back into their half.

The conditions are terrible at the moment. Heavy wind and rain causing havoc.

A lot of set-pieces for Arsenal today as they continue to put Everton under the cosh. Can they take advantage of their dominance again before the break?

Arsenal have found their groove again, with Madueke twice going close to extending their lead. Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard and Merino are forming a box in midfield and Everton don’t seem to know how to shut them down.

Another effort at goal for Madueke. This one is a snapshot from the edge of the box that goes into the side netting.

Madueke should do better. Rice finds him and the winger drives into the box. He takes a shot but drags a right-footed effort wide.

Chance for Arsenal. Rice finds space behind the Everton midfield and drives forward. He plays a pass to Lewis-Skelly, who lays it off to Eze. The England midfielder sidefoots a cross into the box but no one in an Arsenal shirt is there to meet it.

Courtesy of Opta: Arsenal scored their first set-piece goal in all competitions (not including penalties) since May of last season against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one.

George is looking lively for Everton. He tries to come inside and whip an effort to the far corner but the ball deflects wide.

From the corner, Gabriel clears off the line after Raya loses track of the ball.

Everton have responded impressively to the Konsa goal and have been the better team since falling behind. Midfielders Garner and Armstrong are growing into the game quite nicely.

Everton have responded well to going behind here. The early goal against them will have ripped up any plans to sit deep and play on the counter.

Set-pieces are back on the menu for Arsenal. Ezri Konsa’s first goal for the club is their first goal from a corner this season, which will come as a relief to set-piece coach Nicolas Jover. “Set piece again, ole ole,” sing the Arsenal fans. Arteta’s side had started the game on the front foot.

Arsenal had not scored from a corner this season... until now. Konsa breaks the deadlock after a melee in the box and his pokes the ball into the net.

A couple of early set pieces from Declan Rice. Everton do well to clear the danger. But have another one now...

Horrible conditions at the Emirates today. The rain has been lashing down. The Emirates drainage system is usually able to cope with this sort of thing. If the wind picks up, that’s likely to be a bigger problem for the two teams.

After a minute’s applause in honour of Ken Friar, the match makes a prompt start at the Emirates.

“Yeah, we’ve had a good start. Obviously, we had a bit of a blip last week against Chelsea. I don’t think we, as a team, won first and second balls enough and that’s something the manager wants us to get back to today. You’ve got to win your battles.”

On what makes Arsenal difficult to play...

“They’re reigning Premier League champions, a top side that has been knocking on the door to win the title for a few years before as well. They’re a team at a high level but this is what Premier League football is all about and it’s up to us to get a result.”

“Well, we play every two-and-a-half days so we didn’t have much time to recover, so we need full energy. There are certain specific players as well that they fit really well for the game that we expect today and that’s how we start.”

“A very competitive team, a really well organised team. I think that it’s very clear what they want to do, where they want to take the game. The threats, when they have a space to run, any time that they are able to put the ball in their box, you know the presence and aggression that they have. So, yeah, we have to really be at it and be very aggressive from the beginning.”

One of the clearest signs a football club is in a good place is when the debate switches from whether the team are winning to how they are winning.

This is currently Arsenal and Mikel Arteta’s world. For years, Arsenal coaches and players were asked how and when they would start collecting major trophies again. With no concern about their capacity to challenge for top honours over the coming years, the style has become the main focus.

It’s a welcome “problem” – or some might argue a non-existent one – for Arteta while his side is so strong. Building a fortress is the expensive, time-consuming and difficult part. Once it’s constructed and established, how you decorate it is a matter of taste.

Whether neutrals will hold the current champions in the same regard as the great Arsène Wenger sides will be a trivial concern if Arteta does what no Arsenal manager has since 1935 – defend the league title – and then add a few more, which is a serious possibility based on the balance of power in England and the likely punishment heading Manchester City’s way.

Today there will be tributes to Ken Friar, who passed away at the age of 92 earlier this year. Advertising boards outside the Emirates Stadium have been taken over by images of Friar, who had a remarkable 70-year association with the club.

In today’s programme, captain Martin Odegaard has written the following: “It’s exceptional people like Ken Friar who have built the club into what it is today, and we as the current team are the ones privileged to continue his legacy.”

This is a first Premier League start of the season for Viktor Gyokeres, who has been behind Kai Havertz in the pecking order over the past few months. Gyokeres has yet to score in nine appearances in all competitions this season, although he would (understandably) make the point that it’s harder to do so when you are coming off the bench late in games.

For Arsenal, Arteta shuffles his team after the draw against Bayern: White, Lewis-Skelly, Merino, Eze and Gyokeres start.

Max Dowman, who scored a memorable goal in this fixture last season, is on the bench.

For Everton, Jack Grealish misses today’s game due to sickness, while Jarrad Branthwaite is absent because of concussion protocols despite finishing last week’s match with Chelsea after a head collision with Emi Martinez.

Arsenal: Raya, White, Gabriel, Konsa, Lewis-Skelly, Rice, Merino, Odegaard, Madueke, Eze, Gyokeres.Subs: Arrizabalaga, Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori, Mosquera, Zubimendi, Guimaraes, Dowman, Havertz

Everton: Pickford, Tarkowski, O’Brien, Armstrong, Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George, Barry, Garner, Mykolenko, JohnsonSubs: Travers, King, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Dibling, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Braiden Graham

Hello and welcome to coverage from the Emirates as Premier League champions Arsenal host Everton.

Mikel Arteta’s men produced a good performance in midweek to draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League while David Moyes’s squad have had the week off following their 2-0 defeat by Chelsea last weekend.

Arteta said: “We’re having three games in six days so we know what’s happening, especially when the games are so demanding and the necessity is to win. We know that, so we prepare the players for those scenarios and do the best we possibly can.

“I know David so well and how he sets the team, the quality they have in their organisation and individually. It’s no coincidence they didn’t lose before their last game. They have a really good team, which we know because in recent clashes, it’s always been a really difficult game for us.”

Both teams enter this game having been beaten just once this season but eight points separate them with Arsenal in second and Everton in eighth.

Moyes said: “It’s not an easy game and never has been over many years. We look forward to it; they had a game in midweek, and we have to try and capitalise on that. I thought we did really well last year against them; we played really well down at Arsenal, and I hope we can do the same.

“When I look back at the team we had out, we were pretty threadbare at that time, but we did a good job, and I hope we can do it again. Obviously Arsenal have some many different tools in their bag and people they can use in different positions, so we’re fully aware of the team we’re up against and the level.”

Former Arsenal players Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Christian Norgaard could feature for Everton this afternoon.

#1280. When will Italy discover EURO 2028 qualifying opponents?

After missing out on a spot in the Nations League quarter-finals, Italy’s next match will be the first of their EURO 2028 qualifying campaign during the March international break: Here is everything you need to know about the upcoming draw and qualifying process.

Italy will begin their EURO 2028 qualifying campaign during the next international break, which officially kicks off on March 22, 2027.

The Azzurri will learn their EURO 2028 qualifying opponents when the draw takes place in Belfast on Sunday, December 6.

As Italy finished within the top three of the top tier of Nations League groups, they will be among the seeded nations in the EURO 2028 qualifying draw. Joining the Azzurri in the top pot will be France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Greece, Germany, Spain, England, Portugal, Denmark, Norway and Croatia.

There will be 12 qualifying groups in total and given that Italy’s EURO qualifying is now set to get underway in March, they will be placed into a group of five teams rather than four.

Each nation that qualifies at the top of their group, along with the eight-best runners up, will qualify directly for the final tournament.

The four remaining runners up along with the best non-qualified group winners from the 2026-27 Nations League, will be involved in the qualification play-offs for EURO 2028, which will take place in March, 2028.

The number of nations competing in the play-offs depends on the number of host nations that qualify. Between two to four additional spots will be up for grabs in the play-offs, depending on how many of the host nations – England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic or Ireland – qualify directly for the final tournament.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1278. Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, said.

“We got on the front foot and showed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”

Leicester were buoyed in the week by re-signing Jack van Poortfliet, who extended his contract with his boyhood club.

I grew up supporting Leicester, it’s always been my club,” said the England scrum half. This place feels like home in my rugby life. The club is in a really good position, I think we have a great group of lads and great coaches.

I love playing rugby here, I have my best mates here and I believe that we’ve got a group of lads that we can do great things with. I want to be in a place that I love playing for and I believe can win trophies.”

Squally conditions this afternoon at Mattioli Welford Road - in fact make that horrible. An interesting test then for Northampton as lovers of the beautiful game.

You would imagine that the rain and wind would suit a Leicester side whose DNA is set piece power better.

Expect the catch and drive to get plenty of game time and Jack van Poortvliet and Billy Searle to go to the air regularly. It could be a stern examination for teenage Saints full-back James Pater.

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

#1277. Report: Chelsea still interested in Alajbegovic following Man United interest in McKennie

Reports over the weekend claimed that Mauricio Pochettino is keen to bring Weston McKennie with him to Manchester United, and updates on Monday morning claim that Chelsea remain interested in Kerim Alajbegovic, who had been linked with the Blues during the summer transfer window.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, recently-appointed Manchester United coach Pochettino is interested in taking Juventus midfielder McKennie with him to Old Trafford.

The incredibly versatile midfielder has been a key player for the Argentine tactician during his time in charge of the  USA national team and also provides Luciano Spalletti with a number of different possibilities at club level as well.

The Pink Paper is also reporting that Chelsea remain interested in talented teenager Alajbegovic, who had been linked with a move to Stamford Bridge over the summer.

Chelsea had sought after Alajbegovic in the summer and had reportedly proposed a temporary loan move to partner club Strasbourg, but Juventus were eventually able to get a deal over the line with Bayer Leverkusen for a fee of €30m plus up to €5m in bonuses with the promise of regular first-team opportunities.

In the absence of Kenan Yildiz through injury over the first few months of the 2026-27 season, Alajbegovic has received opportunities in the Juventus first team that would have been significantly more difficult to come by with the Premier League club, particularly after splashing around €135m on Morgan Rogers in the same transfer window.

The Bosnian talent has shown glimpses of promise when given the opportunity, but is only six months into his career in Serie A and Juventus are well aware of the youngster’s talent, potential and future value.

As per La Gazzetta dello Sport, Juventus have no intention of selling either Alajbegovic or McKennie, particularly in January, although ‘nothing can be ruled out’ in the event that a monstrous offer arrives from one of the Premier League giants.

Peter Young is a Senior Reporter with Football Italia.

#1274. Thomas Tuchel's 'best night' as England manager: Three Lions boss hails heroes after Spain victory - but hits out at Elliot Anderson decision made by referee he previously labelled a 'one out of 10'

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss

'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'
