#1225. Cubarsí wins 2026 Golden Boy with 475 of 500 points as Barça reach five winners

Barcelona centre-back Pau Cubarsí, 19, has won Tuttosport's 2026 Golden Boy award for Europe's best under-21 player by a wide margin. The landslide puts a defender on top of a prize rarely won by one, and pushes Barcelona further clear as the club with the most winners.

This year’s vote was one-sided. No other candidate came close to the Barcelona defender.

The margin shows how settled the vote was. It also marks a rare win for a player in his position. Corriere dello Sport described him as only the second defender ever to win it. He succeeds PSG’s Désiré Doué, the 2025 winner.

Cubarsí now joins a club list that already featured Messi, Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal. Four of the five have come in the last six years. Pedri won in 2021, Gavi in 2022 and Lamine Yamal in 2024.

No player can win the award twice. Each Barcelona success therefore means a different young player reaching the top of the vote. The recent run points to a steady flow of talent into the first team.

The award caps a strong year for the defender. He was a big part of Barcelona’s LaLiga and Super Cup wins. He was also named young player of the tournament as Spain won the World Cup. He started all eight of Spain’s games there. FIFA’s Young Player Award made him the first defender to receive it. Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final. They kept seven clean sheets and conceded only once, in a 2-1 quarter-final win over Belgium. The Golden Boy arrives just weeks after he narrowly missed out on the Kopa Trophy.

Cubarsí was not the only Barcelona name on the list. Three of Monday’s winners came from the club. Joan Laporta took the Best President award. Barça Femení B’s Giulia Galli won the Best Italian Golden Girl prize. Outside the club, the Best Agent prize went to Jorge Mendes.

Laporta’s prize puts the club’s president alongside its young defender in the same announcement. Galli’s award extends the club’s haul to its women’s set-up. Together, the three prizes give Barcelona recognition across the boardroom, the men’s first team and the women’s game.

— FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 9, 2026

The timing suits both club and country. Barcelona sit top of LaLiga. Spain have a decider against England coming up. For Cubarsí, the award adds individual recognition to a season already built on trophies.

The prizes will be handed out at a ceremony in Turin on 14 December. All three of Barcelona’s awards become official at that ceremony.

They will be taken at The Kop. Chelsea goalkeeper Penders disappeared down the tunnel after the full-time whistle and re-emerges with a towel, potentially some penalty-saving notes as well?

Liverpool will take first and it will be Mac Allister who steps up first...

The final whistle is blown so we go to penalties at Anfield.

Looks like we are heading for penalties and if you are looking for omens... Liverpool and Chelsea have had four shootouts in the past: Liverpool won them all - the 2007 Champions League semi-final, the 2019 European Super Cup final, the 2022 League Cup final and the 2022 FA Cup Final.

A word on VAR (again). Watching this competition without the presence of the joy-killing invention is liberating. An occassional decision might get missed but, in the long term, you could live with that if meant you didn’t hear the words “it’s being checked by Stockley Park”. The decision just before, when Florian Wirtz’s shot touched Levi Colwill’s hand, was a case in point. It wasn’t a penalty but VAR being brought into play might convince you it was. Let’s get rid of it, please.

Double change for Liverpool as Isak and Mac Allister replace Ngumoha and Nyoni.

Huge double block from Chelsea and how have Liverpool not scored? Tsimikas’ cross to the back post is headed back across the six-yard box to find Wirtz, who you think is going to score but Colwill makes the block. Then Barcola has a shot blocked by Acheampong.

It is full time at both Craven Cottage and the Stadium of Light, where Crystal Palace and Sunderland have booked their places in the League Cup quarter-finals.

Tsimikas gives it away inside his own half and Chelsea counter. Neto drives inside and finds Rogers, who skips past Gomez. Rogers then finds the overlapping Palestra on the left side of the box and the Italian is denied by Mamardashvili at his near post.

Manchester City have just beaten Brighton 4-3 on penalties whilst on the south coast Bournemouth have comfortably beaten Aston Villa 3-0. Both sides are into the hat for tonight’s quarter-final draw.

Lavia cynically brings down Ngumoha as the Liverpool forward drove through the Chelsea half and is correctly booked.

Liverpool are taking off Van Dijk and Jacquet is coming on in his place. No injury for Van Dijk.

What a terrific cup tie this has been. It helps when there is an edge between the sides and you can feel the tension in the air. What has been noticeable in the last three games at Anfield, though, is the change in the atmosphere. Slowly but surely the locals are buying into what Andoni Iraola is trying to achieve. Liverpool could lose this game tonight by going all out to win it but there is a clearly identity developing that makes you think they are starting to get on the right lines.

After Gakpo fouls Lavia, Chelsea have a free-kick just over 25 yards out. Rogers lines it up but his effort is terrible, flying into The Kop.

Chelsea are going to make a triple change. Palestra, Barco and Emegha come on, with the latter on for his Chelsea debut. Gusto, Caicedo and Welbeck head off.

Good save from Penders. The ball comes to Barcola outside the Chelsea penalty area. The Frenchman drives inside before getting his shot away from the edge of the box. The shot takes a small deflection and Penders does well to make the save down to his left.

The game between Manchester City and Brighton at The Etihad has ended 2-2, therefore it has now gone to penalties.

Chances at both ends. Gomez whips in a cross from the right and picks out Araujo in the centre of the box but the Uruguayan’s powerful header is straight at Penders. He probably should have scored.

Then Chelsea counter and Rogers is in acres of space. His shot from just outside the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Gusto’s behaviour in recent minutes has been appalling. First he went down after virtually no contact from Van Dijk and now goes down again, once more not a foul. He shows his boot to the linesman as if it came off in a challenge from Barcola but the replays show that his boot did not come off and he was attempting to con the officials.

Andoni Iraola is turning to his bench for the first time tonight and makes a double substitution as Wirtz and Barcola replace McConnell and Koumas. Some double change that for Liverpool!

Fascinating to watchg Trey Nyoni and the responsibility he has taken on his shoulders. He’s only 19 but those who have worked with him since he arrived at Liverpool as a 16-year-old will tell you he has a maturity of someone in their mid-twenties. He has tried to get on the ball and play, he’s been strong when it’s been required and always been in the right place to get a foot in. He’s going to play a lot of games for Liverpool if he maintains this trajectory.

Achemapong scythes Ngumoha down as the latter cut inside and the former is correctly booked.

Down on the south coast, Bournemouth appear to be cruising into the quarter-finals as Alvaro Rodriguez has put them 3-0 up against Aston Villa.

Should Rogers have done better there? In fortuitous circumstances, he is played through but he does not show the conviction to drive towards the Liverpool penalty area. His touch lets him and the ball rolls through to Mamardashvili.

Moments later, Rogers forces Mamadrashvili into a save to his left and the Liverpool players are furious that a handball was not given. It clearly hit Rogers’ arm before he shot but Chelsea do have the corner. Chelsea play it short before eventually Henderson swings it in before Araujo heads away.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Manchester City have equalised at home against Brighton, with Rayan Cherki’s free-kick from just outside the box taking a big deflection off his teammate Vitor Reis and ending up in the back ot the Brighton net.

Manchester City 1 Brighton 2 (70’)Bournemouth 2 Aston Villa 0 (58’)Fulham 0 Crystal Palace 1 (56’)Sunderland 3 Brentford 1 (56’)Liverpool 1 Chelsea 1 HT

Bournemouth have doubled their advantage against Aston Villa through Lewis Cook just over five minutes into the second half.

Possession: Liverpool 50%-50% ChelseaShots: 6-2Shots on target: 2-1Corners: 5-0Touches in opposition box: 5-9

The first half is brought to an end at Anfield and the game is level at 1-1 going into the break. Rogers put Chelsea in front from the spot only for Gakpo to also score a penalty moments later to equalise for Liverpool.

The outswinging corner is sent in from the left but Araujo’s header goes over the bar. Meanwhile, Lacroix is slowly limping his way around the pitch to the tunnel and is moving very gingerly, which could suggest an extended period on the sidelines.

As we enter three minutes of added time, Colwill replaces the injured Lacroix.

Liverpool can sense a second goal. First, Gakpo has a shot saved by Penders before Ngumoha wins the hosts a corner. Before that is taken, play has been stopped as Lacroix is down clutching at his left hamstring.

Not a murmur from Xabi Alonso as his side take the lead. The penalty Morgan Rogers dispatched went in the same corner as Alonso picked in the 2007 Champions League semi-final and perhaps he had a sense of what was coming as Liverpool are now level and it’s a fair reflection of how an intriguing opening 45 minutes has played out. It really wouldn’t be a surprise if we need spot-kicks to separate these teams at 90 minutes.

Like Rogers moments ago, Gakpo sends the goalkeeper the wrong way and puts the penalty away to equalise. Gakpo slots into the bottom left corner in front of The Kop and the Dutchman continues his fine scoring record in this competition. Both sides have been gifted penalties and both teams take advantage.

Cody Gakpo slots home a penalty to equalise for Liverpool against Chelsea! 💪 https://t.co/rS775LH0Gb

Like London buses, two penalties come in quick succession. From a Liverpool corner out on the left, Fofana is penalised for a handball and the referee has no choice but to point to the spot. The Chelsea players protest but it clearly hit Fofana’s arm, which was above his head.

Rogers sends Mamardashvili the wrong way and puts Chelsea 1-0 up in front of their travelling supporters. It was a quality penalty from Rogers, who deposited it into the right corner of the goal. It is a gift for Chelsea, who did not look like scoring but are gifted a chance to score through that silly Gravenberch challenge.

Morgan Rogers puts Chelsea in front against Liverpool from the spot! 🎯 https://t.co/ocMXFNCW9F

Caicedo goes down inside the Liverpool penalty area and the referee points to the spot. It is a silly and needless challenge from Gravenberch, who slides into the back of Caicedo and gives the referee no choice but to give a penalty. Not that it would be overturned but there is no VAR anyway.

Ex-Liverpool man Henderson was holding the ball for a while but now hands over to Rogers to take...

They are into the second half at Manchester and Brighton have retaken the lead through Georginio Rutter. Brighton now lead Manchester City 2-1.

That is a gift from Chelsea. The communication at the back between Gusto and Fofana is poor, with the former playing a poor pass backwards looking for Fofana, who cannot reach it and the ball rolls behind for the easiest of corners for Liverpool in front of The Kop.

Gakpo takes an outswinging corner but Welbeck is on hand to head away at the front post.

We are yet to see the first goal of the night at Anfield but they are flying in at the Stadium of Light. Brentford have pulled a goal back against Sunderland through Callum Wilson and it is now 3-1 in the north east.

Chelsea want a penalty. Rogers goes down inside the Liverpool penalty area under a challenge from Araujo but it was a fair shoulder-to-shoulder challenge and that is not a penalty.

At the Stadium of Light, Sunderland are in dreamland. Malick Fofana has put them 3-0 up against Brentford closing in on half-time.

A wasted free kick from Chelsea, and goodness, Austin McPhee is not happy. Chelsea’s set piece coach was up on the touchline, remonstrating to nobody in particular but it was obvious to see the frustration that the plan he has worked on - a chip to the side, a cutback into the middle - has fallen down at the first attempt. To compound his fury, McPhee just blew a gasket after Chelsea were not awarded a penalty following a coming together between Ronald Araujo and Morgan Rogers.

Tsimikas has let Ngumoha down there. Ngumoha does brilliantly to dribble through two Chelsea defenders around the halfway line and drives down the left. He then plays the ball outside to Tsimikas, who should do so much better with his cross but picks out the front-post defender Lacroix.

Meanwhile at Craven Cottage, Crystal Palace have taken the lead at Fulham thanks to Eddie Nketiah.

McConnell becomes the second Liverpool player to be booked tonight for handball. He lost the ball on halfway and cynically handled the ball as Rogers attempted to counter. A fairly clear-cut booking for McConnell there.

A reminder that there is no VAR tonight and if the game is level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. Referee Darren England has summoned Chelsea captain Caicedo and former Liverpool midfielder Henderson over for a word.

Caicedo puts Tsimikas’ cross from the left behind for the first corner of the night. Gakpo sends in the inswinger but the whistle goes as Chelsea are awarded a free-kick for a foul from Tsimikas on Gusto.

There has yet to be a goal at Anfield but at the Stadium of Light Sunderland have doubled their lead over Brentford courtesy of Tymur Tutierov’s goal.

The first booking of the night at Anfield goes the way of the home side. Koumas slides in to try and block a clearance from Lacroix and is booked. Koumas barely touched Lacroix and that is never a yellow card.

Meanwhile, in the north east, Sunderland have taken the lead against Brentford through Chemsdine Talbi.

Brighton had led in Manchester but the home side have just equalised. Mateo Kovacic has scored from range to bring Manchester City level with five minutes to go in the first half.

Clear to see in these early exchanges that Cody Gakpo has been deployed as Liverpool’s main “striker” with Lewis Koumas, James McConnell - who played in the 2024 final when Liverpool beat Chelsea 1-0 - and Rio Ngumoha operating in behind him. Jordan Henderson seems to be the man whom Xabi Alonso wants to trigger Chelsea’s press. They are playing a rigid 4-5-1 formation but, this being Alonso, the system is always flexible. His ethos is to be able to play two or three systems in a game if needed.

Ngumoha drives at Neto down Liverpool’s left and is felled by the Portuguese forward. It is an obvious free-kick and Neto is a touch fortunate not to be booked for that blatant foul. Ngumoha, who was fantastic for Liverpool against Villarreal in the Champions League just over a week ago, already into the action.

Tsimikas clips in the delivery but it is headed away by Lacroix.

The second goal in the League Cup this evening has come in Manchester and has gone the way of the away side. Malick Yalcouye has put Brighton in front against Manchester City on the half-hour mark.

We are under way at Anfield. Who will book their place in the League Cup quarter-finals; Liverpool or Chelsea?

Jordan Henderson is busily going around geeing up Chelsea’s players, in exactly the same fashion as he did when he played in this stadium for 12 years. He got an ovation here in May, when Brentford drew 1-1, that left him extremely emotional but it remains to be seen what will happen when he gets his first touch this evening. There has been no acknowledgement - yet - from The Kop and the same is true for Xabi Alonso. But, then again, why would there be when there is such lingering enmity between these clubs?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off at Anfield. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Liverpool: Mamardashvili; Araujo, Gomez, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; McConnell, Nyoni; Ngumoha, Gravenberch, Gakpo; KoumasSubstitutes: Alisson, Endo, Jacquet, Wirtz, Isak, Mac Allister, Chiesa, Barcola, Chambers.

Chelsea: Penders; Acheampong, Lacroix, Fofana, Gusto, Caicedo, Lavia, Henderson, Neto, Welbeck, Rogers.Substitutes: Sharman-Lowe, Colwill, Subuloye, Palestra, Barco, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estevao, Quenda, Emegha.

Has come on the south coast, where Bournemouth have taken the lead against Aston Villa courtesy of Amine Adli’s goal inside the opening 10 minutes.

“The cups are important for us this year. For sure, we face today a good challenge, coming to Anfield, and we want to be in the next round. It is another competition. We know it is another format, it is make-or-break, so we want to make it happen today with a great performance.

“From the beginning we have taken it seriously. We have a tough game and we want to have a good feeling that we are competing. We have to do many great things. In one game there can be many little games with the energy created. These players have played here before. We have practiced penalties but sometimes it is about the feeling of the day.”

The games at the Vitality Stadium, Craven Cottage and the Stadium of Light have just begun. That means four of the five ties tonight have started, with just the game at Anfield to begin in just over 10 minutes.

At The Etihad, Manchester City have kicked off against Brighton. Then, there are three 7.45pm kick-offs before Liverpool begin against Chelsea at Anfield at 8pm.

"I have trust that they can perform well" Andoni Iraola on giving youth a chance in his Liverpool side to face Chelsea 🔴 https://t.co/5Z9xoGgqHz

More than two years have passed since Rio Ngumoha chose to leave Chelsea for Liverpool, but the frustration remains at Stamford Bridge. The pain of losing a player of Ngumoha’s potential does not pass quickly, especially as the winger was part of Chelsea’s academy system for eight years. It must sting to see a London boy, one of their own, now delighting the Anfield crowd.

For many at Chelsea, the anger at Ngumoha’s departure in 2024 will probably never subside. Or, at least, it will not subside while he continues to develop so thrillingly at Liverpool. Such was Chelsea’s annoyance at the time of his exit, Telegraph Sport reported last year, Liverpool’s scouts were subsequently banned from attending matches at their academy centre.

Xabi Alonso spent five years as a player at Anfield between 2004 and 2009. He has returned twice as an opposition manager, with both ending in defeats; one as Bayer Leverkusen boss and one as Real Madrid manager.

Boss. 👋 #CFC | #CarabaoCup https://t.co/XwweYtU2Ae

All five games this evening are all-Premier League ties:

Manchester City vs Brighton 7.30pmBournemouth vs Aston Villa 7.45pmFulham vs Crystal Palace 7.45pmSunderland vs Brentford 7.45pmLiverpool vs Chelsea 8pm

The two sides already into the hat for the quarter-finals are Bradford and Fleetwood, who knocked Arsenal out last night. The draw for the quarter-finals will take place after tonight’s matches.

Tonight's Blues. ✊💙 #CFC | #CarabaoCup https://t.co/Q7pTQHkgDc

Come on you Reds ✊🔴 https://t.co/o9Rc2yjV7c

It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola said ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”

Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike remain long-term absentees for the hosts with Jeremie Frimpong also missing. Florian Wirtz could feature despite going off with an ankle knock during the win over Brighton.

Like Liverpool, Chelsea also had an all-Premier League tie in the third round of this competition, beating Leeds 6-3 in a high-scoring affair at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea come into tonight’s game off the back of a 2-0 defeat against Tottenham in the league last weekend. Not only did they lose on Saturday but to make matters worse for them Cole Palmer was sent off. As a result of that red card, Palmer is suspended for tonight’s tie.

“We [Alonso and Palmer] spoke and for sure he knows the mistake he made,” Alonso said. “Things that you can avoid. I hope that this is not going to be repeated. He is aware of that, he is mature and it was a mistake. He is in a good space, he connects very well socially with his teammates. They like him, they want Cole smiling, they want Cole having fun, enjoying his game because when we see that, he will have a better team. I will just ask you because he has got this very cool persona, you probably know his personality is very interesting.”

Former Liverpool midfielder and current Chelsea boss Alonso has lost his two games as a manager against Liverpool; a 4-0 defeat as Bayer Leverkusen boss and then a 1-0 loss when in charge of Real Madrid, with both taking place at Anfield. Alonso is not the only ex-Liverpool midfielder to return to Anfield tonight as their former captain Jordan Henderson is in the Chelsea squad for tonight. Joao Pedro has missed the trip to Anfield because of a thigh injury which could rule him out for a few weeks.

The Premier league fixture between these sides at Anfield ended in a 1-1 draw back in May. In that match, Arne Slot was in charge of Liverpool with Calum McFarlane in interim charge of Chelsea. Chelsea won the reverse fixture 2-1 at Stamford Bridge. Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

#1223. With Manchester United set to hire Mauricio Pochettino, what other managers are available?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Manchester United have decided to make a managerial change during the November international break and sacked Michael Carrick after a challenging start to the season. The Red Devils have reportedly decided to hire Mauricio Pochettino, who led the United States men's national team at the 2026 World Cup and just signed a new deal with the American federation. However, Pochettino had a $10 million release clause in his contract and spoke multiple times about his desire to go back to the English Premier League, after coaching Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea before making his move to the U.S.

Manchester United have also explored multiple options in the past weeks, and several names emerged as potential candidates for the job. Let's take a look at the top free-agent coaches currently available on the market and identify those who remain open to a move in the near future. For this specific reason we have decided to not include former Manchester City coach Pep Guardiola, who is not looking for a job in the short term.

The Spanish coach left Manchester City ahead of the summer of 2026 and decided to take a break from the world of soccer, despite having a concrete offer in the summer to become the new manager of the Italian national team. Guardiola sat down with the Italian federation but then opted to stick to his commitment to take a break. Furthermore, given his close ties to the Manchester City hierarchy and ownership, his name was never going to be considered by the Manchester United board. Here's a list of the top coaches without a job right now:

The former England national team manager is still searching for his next club after deciding to step down from his international role in order to return to club management. However, he appears unlikely to find a new position in the short term. This is a challenge currently facing several national team coaches, including former France manager Didier Deschamps. Manchester United had previously shown interest in him, but did not make a concrete approach in recent weeks, despite having the opportunity to do so.

The former Tottenham manager was one of the names that emerged in the past weeks for the Man United job. However, the former Brentford and Spurs manager is now in talks to become the new Crystal Palace manager after a disappointing start to the Premier League season, as the Eagles are currently at the bottom of the standings, two points behind Manchester United.

The former Newcastle head coach was one of the names on the list of the Manchester United board of directors in recent weeks. The English head coach left Newcastle in the summer and he's still under contract with the club right now. Any club looking to appoint him would first have to pay a release clause to Newcastle. Despite his Premier League experience, Manchester United did not consider him as a potential replacement. He is now likely to wait until the summer before deciding on his next career move.

An attractive name: the former German national team coach left his job in the summer after the disappointment of the 2026 World Cup, when Germany were kicked out by Paraguay in the round of 32 of the tournament. Nagelsmann, after coaching RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich before moving to the national team, is now likely to move to another league, and the Premier League is definitely a league that can potentially attract him. Let's now see if there will be a job available in the summer, even if the big clubs seem pretty stable at this stage.

The Italian coach is waiting for the right opportunity to come after the two years spent at Napoli, where he was able to win the Scudetto in his first season in charge, replicating the success he had at Juventus and Inter in his home country. According to reports, Conte would be keen for another Premier League experience after coaching Chelsea and Tottenham but he's not ruling out other clubs. However, Manchester United never made contact with his camp as they didn't want to hire the Italian manager to replace Carrick. Conte has often been regarded as a short-term appointment, having never spent more than three years at any single club throughout his managerial career.

#1222. Salty grains in Saturn’s outermost ring formed from the slow freeze of plumes from the moon Enceladus

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Kevin P. Hand is at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Pasadena, California 91109, USA.

Saturn is surrounded by eight rings of ice and rock fragments, with the E ring being the outermost one. Supplied with material mainly by the erupting ice plumes of Enceladus, one of Saturn’s moons, the E ring continues to inform studies of planetary science and astrobiology. Now, nine years after the Cassini spacecraft transmitted its last gasp of data from Saturn back to Earth, Postberg et al.1 report in Science Advances the latest analysis of the grains that make up the E ring. They also discuss what these data can tell us about the subsurface ocean of Enceladus, including whether it could be habitable.

#1221. Blázquez double from Rioja assists seals Valencia’s 6-0 Copa del Rey win over Tavernes

Aimar Blázquez scored twice from Rioja assists as Valencia beat Tavernes 6-0 at Mestalla, where the hosts were officially the away side. The win follows a 0-3 defeat to Real Madrid and takes Valencia into the second round.

Valencia cruised past Tavernes in the Copa del Rey on Tuesday 10 November 2026. The tie was played at the Estadio de Mestalla, yet Valencia were officially the away side in their own stadium. The RFEF had granted Tavernes’ request to stage the match there.

Raba opened the scoring in the first minute, with Blázquez providing the assist. Raba then turned provider for Duro in the 11th minute. Rioja added the third in the 19th minute after a pass from Martinez. A fourth goal arrived through Elliott in the 23rd minute.

Tavernes goalkeeper Mainar kept the margin there three minutes into the second half. He saved a header from Blázquez, who had been set up by Raba. The number 37 struck in the 57th minute and again in the 69th. Danjuma replaced him after 70 minutes, when Gayà also came on for Rioja.

Three players were booked. Ugrinic was cautioned in the ninth minute and Montilla of Tavernes in the 22nd. Rioja picked up a yellow card in the 49th minute.

Tavernes came closest to a goal when Erik struck the post after a short corner. EFE described the visitors as a sixth-tier club and reported that close to 40 coaches carried their fans to Mestalla. Their municipal ground was not fit for the tie. Mestalla is in its final season before the move to Nou Mestalla.

A 9pm start had been planned for the tie. Every Copa del Rey match scheduled for that day was called off by the RFEF, and this one was among them.

Tavernes reached the first round through the two-legged preliminary round against UD Maracena. The first leg was played at the CD Maracena ground on Sunday 27 September 2026. The two sides drew 1-1 and 0-0.

For Valencia, the Real Madrid loss had itself followed a 1-0 win over Elche and a 1-2 defeat to Villarreal. Javier Aguirre said he took positive conclusions from the tie. He welcomed the return of players who had been out long-term. He also said Valencia now need to win in the league.

Aimar Blazquez scored a brace for Valencia as they pummeled Tavernes to advance to the next round of the Spanish Copa Del Rey pic.twitter.com/sgzCjeOecT

— Football with Osadolor (@osa_dolor) November 11, 2026

The cup calendar continues with the round of 32 on 16 December. The last 16 follows on 6 January and the quarter-finals on 13 January. The semi-finals are the only two-legged round, with first legs on 10 February and second legs on 3 March. The competition runs until 24 April 2027.

Valencia return to league action away to Rayo Vallecano at the Estadio de Vallecas on Saturday 21 November.

#1220. Inside Gotham FC's move to Icahn Stadium: Debates over pitch quality, fines and the NWSL's logistical struggle

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Juan Carlos Amoros is always subtle in demeanor, down to his usual all-black attire, so after Gotham FC's uninspiring 1-0 win over the Seattle Reign on Sunday, his subdued tone was hardly a surprise. His post-match remarks, though, were a departure from the victory lap a coach might take after winning in the NWSL quarterfinals.

"I feel the obligation to almost apologize for the state of the pitch," Amoros said. "I think at this level, in this kind of game, as a league, we should be having a better surface. Unfortunately, our football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn't but luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt and the game was what it was."

He was hardly the only one to mention the grass at Sports Illustrated Stadium. It seeped its way into every post-match media availability, dominated conversation between the players and was a talking point amongst staff working that day. A dull stretch of grass with yellow-green splotches overshadowed one of the most important matches of the NWSL's season – and put the league on course for an unlikely downsize for Sunday's playoff semifinal between Gotham and the Kansas City Current.

Roughly 24 hours after Amoros' apology, Gotham moved Sunday's game to Icahn Stadium, a 5,000-seater on Manhattan's Randall's Island that they have played at just twice before. Sports Illustrated Stadium, the 25,000-seat venue in Harrison, N.J. that Gotham have called home since 2021, was available but concerns about player safety prompted an unwanted last-minute move.

"We as a team worked extremely hard to earn a home playoff berth," Gotham captain Tierna Davidson said in a statement on Monday. "What we got was a field that is not the standard this club, this league or our fans deserve. The quality of the game is not up for debate, so we've made the difficult decision to move to Icahn Stadium on Sunday. A smaller stadium means many of you will not be there, and that is the hardest part of this decision."

Monday's announcement was the final stage of a back-and-forth between Gotham and MLS' Red Bull New York, the primary tenants and operators of Sports Illustrated Stadium, one that highlights the logistical nightmares that have unexpectedly disrupted the NWSL's postseason.

MLS' World Cup break this summer afforded RBNY the chance to install a new pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, the process complete by the team's July 25 loss to Charlotte FC. It was the perfect time for a reset ahead of a busy schedule for the new field – 17 other matches were a guarantee, while the potential postseason runs for both RBNY and Gotham meant the number could stretch well over 20 games before the year was over.

By the time Gotham had secured a home quarterfinal with a draw against Angel City on Oct. 4, there was little reason to suspect that the playing surface would become an issue. Matches are rarely relocated because of pitch quality concerns and the field at Sports Illustrated Stadium has historically been one of American soccer's best; it won the Sports Turf Management Association's award for professional soccer fields in 2021, the year Gotham moved in. The NWSL team did not have another home game until Nov. 1, a period in which RBNY played three home games and the stadium hosted a USA Rugby Fall Series doubleheader. Sometime before the early November fixture against the Royals, Gotham raised concerns with their landlords about the field conditions, the scars of the rugby games on Oct. 30 notably visible.

Nothing came of those complaints, though, and so the Royals match went on as scheduled but the conditions did not go unnoticed. The NWSL imposed a $10,000 fine on Gotham for the state of the field, even though they do not manage the venue as secondary tenants. The fine was not widely known – the NWSL Players Association said it was unaware of the punishment, while a source with knowledge of the matter said RBNY also did not know. Many found out about the fine after Reign head coach Laura Harvey mentioned it in a post-match press conference after the quarterfinal, but worry about the quality of the grass had already reached a fever pitch at that point.

Despite the fine, a field consultant working on the NWSL's behalf inspected the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium on Friday and declared that it met FIFA standards. The following day, RBNY hosted their regular season finale against Atlanta United and less than 18 hours later, another group took a look at the field in the hours building up to Gotham's win over the Reign. It was deemed playable on Sunday morning by representatives from the NWSL, the Professional Referee Organization and the NWSLPA, according to a source familiar with the situation.

Even from a distance, the grass appeared problematic. The sand that was left over from the rugby doubleheader still lined the pitch, while some rugby lines were faint but visible in certain spots. The players' review of the surface, though, was damning – Harvey called it "s---," Reign captain Jess Fishlock said it was "atrocious," and Gotham midfielder Jaelin Howell described it as "sandy" and "unstable." Gotham attacker Jaedyn Shaw also expressed concern that her planted foot would slip during corner kicks and all agreed that it ultimately impacted the teams' ability to compete.

lower bowl isn’t quite full at kickoff between Gotham and the Seattle Reign, though there are some fans in the upper bowlGotham announced earlier that they sold 3,000 tickets through NYC Mayor Mamdani’s offer (including 1,000 in the first 10 minutes of sale)#NWSL pic.twitter.com/qviBM65bsz

Gotham, in conjunction with the NWSL, spent the hours after their quarterfinal win discussing options with RBNY to improve the playing surface. The main solutions, according to multiple sources, were re-sodding the pitch – essentially ripping the existing field out and installing a new one – or a hybrid model in which artificial threads would be stitched into the existing grass. Both would be timely endeavors – the former would be longer while the latter might have been completed in time for Gotham to host the Current on Sunday.

There was just one problem. RBNY have a friendly against Club America scheduled for Saturday.

The game will serve as the final match of their season after they missed the MLS Cup playoffs and takes place during the men's international break, which means some players from both teams will be tied up with their national teams instead. Multiple sources said the NWSL could not guarantee that the hybrid model project would not actually be completed in time for RBNY's friendly on Saturday evening, even if it would have been ready in time for Gotham's Sunday afternoon game against the Current. RBNY were unwilling to proceed with the hybrid plan, as a result, and so Gotham chose to leave Sports Illustrated Stadium for Icahn Stadium.

RBNY still intend to play on the pitch that NWSL players complained about on Saturday and no changes to the field are expected to be made beforehand.

"We understand how frustrating the move is for Gotham and their fans. We had hoped to see Gotham continue its championship run at Sports Illustrated Stadium, too," RBNY said in a statement. "We invest in the pitch year-round, with a dedicated grounds team and specialist field partners, and it was cleared for every match played there this season. Those inspections continue for all remaining events this year. We worked closely with Gotham and the NWSL to address their concerns, but unfortunately the experts and the league couldn't guarantee the additional work they wanted to be completed could be done in time. We wish Gotham the best in their match."

The venue is not brand new to Gotham, who have hosted two games at the stadium in the last two years, and seems well-equipped to at least solve the main problem they faced at Sports Illustrated Stadium. Amoros complimented the quality of Icahn Stadium's pitch when Gotham hosted a Concacaf W Champions Cup group stage game there in Aug. 2025. Though it did not prompt Gotham's selection of Icahn Stadium to host that match, the New Jersey venue's field had also looked suboptimal in the run-up to the continental clash. RBNY subsequently replaced the pitch during that period, weeks before the U.S. men's national team played a friendly against South Korea on Sept. 6 last year.

"I don't really want to talk too much about it but the Sports Illustrated Stadium has traditionally been the best pitch in the league," Amoros said at the time, "and the last couple of games, it's definitely been far away from that so this pitch here is outstanding."

Gotham's last-minute switch to Icahn Stadium was a surprise in large part because an entirely separate scheduling issue had overshadowed the first week of the postseason.

The NWSL had two broadcast slots for the semifinals, Saturday at noon ET on CBS and Sunday at 3 p.m. ET on ABC, but did not exactly have the first-choice venues to host them. RBNY's Saturday friendly locked Gotham out of that time slot entirely if they wanted to play at Sports Illustrated Stadium, but they needed the Washington Spirit to beat the Portland Thorns for the Sunday window since the Thorns would be unable to hold a game that kicked off at 9 a.m. local time. The Spirit's lopsided win guaranteed Gotham would play on Sunday but they had their own issues – the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III college football game between the United States Merchant Marine Academy and the United States Coast Guard Academy, was taking place at Audi Field during the Saturday time slot.

The Spirit seemed destined for a semifinal at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., home of the NFL's Washington Commanders and a stadium they had never played in before, but late discussions with Audi Field's owners, MLS' D.C. United, and a contribution from sponsor Lafayette Federal Credit Union to underwrite the costs of the schedule change meant that problem was solved.

Gotham's move to Icahn Stadium, though, only reinforced the logistical issues that the NWSL has battled for its entire existence. The optics have favored the league in recent years, with the vast majority of their teams playing in state-of-the-art soccer-specific stadiums and managing to survive the constant game of venue Tetris. Scheduling conflicts, though, were never out of the realm of possibility, and many have marred the league this year. The Boston Legacy, for example, had to move home games from Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass. to Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket, R.I., during the World Cup and will play there in 2027 while the construction project continues on Boston's White Stadium.

The issues that plagued Gotham and the Spirit, though, are in line with a different problem – control over facilities. Around half of the league's teams are secondary tenants in the stadiums they play in, so management of the venues is almost entirely out of their hands. It is unclear how quickly that will change for any of those teams. Gotham will leave Sports Illustrated Stadium for Etihad Park in 2028, but that stadium will be managed by MLS' New York City FC. They will continue to be secondary tenants in that building, which technically means they could be subject to the same problems they currently face. MLS' calendar flip next year will likely see the issue morph but not necessarily change. The leagues' postseason schedules will be different for the foreseeable future but teams like Gotham and the Spirit will still be at the mercy of their landlords in the meantime; Gotham's conflict with RBNY an example of just that. RBNY's friendly was the sticking point in their discussions over the pitch and ultimately took precedence over an NWSL semifinal.

Control over venues continues to weigh heavily in the NWSL's expansion process and is a key part of the issue that causes the most hand-wringing in the league's front office – the calendar. The Current might be the NWSL's gold standard as the owners and operators of CPKC Stadium, though they have been hamstrung by the NWSL's scheduling issues. Kickoff of their quarterfinal win over Angel City was at 11:30 a.m. local time because they were the only team able to take that broadcast slot on CBS. The since-ousted San Diego Wave could not host a game with a 9:30 a.m. local kickoff, while Gotham and the Spirit were locked out of their venues because of MLS matches on the same day.

There is a meet-in-the-middle approach, one that the NWSL might use as often as they can as the expansion process continues. A handful of teams share ownership groups with MLS teams, who chiefly own and operate their own stadiums and tend to treat the NWSL teams as equal tenants. The number will grow in 2028 when teams in Atlanta and Columbus, both owned by the local MLS clubs, will join the league.

#1219. The four problems Mauricio Pochettino needs to fix at Man United: From big names causing unrest in the dressing room to an issue which plagued Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick before him, these are the items top of his Old Trafford in-tray

Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 10:51 EST, 14 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino will see out his final two games as US national team boss with a double-header against Haiti before starting work at Manchester United on Wednesday.

The 54-year-old won’t have any time to waste with a daunting first game against United’s bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday followed by a European clash with Sporting Lisbon in Portugal three days later.

With United languishing in the Premier League relegation zone and 17th in the Champions League standings, it’s clear why Pochettino has been brought in to replace Michael Carrick on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the most pressing matters in Pochettino’s in-tray at Carrington as the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss and his backroom staff head for Manchester...

Mauricio Pochettino is the new manager of Manchester United - but the problems he has to fix are already piling up

It sounds obvious, but winning games to get United out of the Premier League drop zone has to be the first priority.

Everything at a football club flows from the results on the pitch, and United’s humiliating decline this season has had ramifications throughout Old Trafford and Carrington.

The players are clearly low on confidence which has only exacerbated the team’s dismal performances and brought just one win in 10 Premier League games, against newly-promoted Ipswich – United’s worst start in 40 years.

Diogo Dalot is a prime example, after fans cheered his substitution in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend, and the defender cut a crestfallen figure as he left Old Trafford to go on international duty with Portugal.

The Stretford End also turned on the players as the atmosphere turned toxic after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth at the end of last month, having vented their anger towards the club’s ownership – the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – as well as chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox at every opportunity.

That won’t go away anytime soon, but a winning team will at least take some of the sting out of the situation if appointing Pochettino can give United a ‘bounce’ and divert attention back onto the pitch.

United players are low on confidence, not least Diogo Dalot (left) whose substitution was cheered by his own fans against Aston Villa

The United team were also lambasted by the Stretford End after the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth last month

Carrick enjoyed a good start, losing just two of his 17 games in charge in the second half of last season to earn a two-year contract, but United struggled under him this term due to a combination of poor recruitment, injuries and lack of fitness.

These are all issues that Pochettino must try to put right. There is little he can do about recruitment until the January transfer window opens and United have a chance to atone for their mistake in not signing cover at left back and centre forward last summer, which backfired spectacularly when both Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko picked up injuries.

He can, however, try to get more out of United’s £155million midfield signings Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again – Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, and a United squad that was good enough to finish third in the Premier League last season.

Injuries have been a major problem with the hamstring strain that will keep Baleba out of action for Pochettino’s first few weeks in charge just the latest setback.

As well as Shaw, Sesko, Baleba and long-term casualty Manuel Ugarte, United have also lost Amad Diallo, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martinez, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui for parts of this season.

Pochettino must get more out of United’s £155million midfield signing Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again

United have struggled to keep up with their opponents since the opening day - a lack of fitness has plagued every manager since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer

The good news for Pochettino is that Shaw and Rashford are hoping to be fit for Anfield, while Matthijs de Ligt is available again after a year out with back problems. However, Sesko’s absence until the new year leaves the new boss without his most natural source of goals.

Fitness is another matter and United have looked short of it since the opening-day defeat at Hull City amid concerns that the coaching levels dropped off under Carrick and were too relaxed.

They covered 120.8 kilometres against Villa – the most in a league game under Carrick – and Pochettino will demand that and a whole lot more as he increases the work-rate among his new squad.

It’s a problem that has hindered a succession of United bosses going back to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, and the Argentine must find a way to drill a better work ethic into United.

The problems at United this season have inevitably led to unrest in the dressing room, with the biggest issue centred around captain Bruno Fernandes.

News that Fernandes has rejected United’s latest contract offer has come as no surprise given his dramatic change in fortunes from last season, and Pochettino must find a way to get arguably United’s best player back in form and onside.

Having set a new Premier League record for assists and picked up a string of player of the year awards last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off a cliff as he struggled with an injury sustained at the World Cup, and he suffered the rare indignity of being benched for the loss to Bournemouth.

Never one to hide his mood very well, the 32-year-old criticised Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat by Como in what was a major blow to his head coach.

Never one to hide his mood very well, Bruno Fernandes has been disgruntled of late and rejected United's offer of a new contract

Lisandro Martinez looks to be headed for the exit door - although the arrival of his fellow Argentine Pochettino may help things

While the United hierarchy will try to persuade Fernandes to sign a new deal in keeping with their reduced wage structure and the fact he will turn 33 next year, Pochettino has to find a way of relighting the fire in his skipper.

Whether the club will make as much effort to keep Lisandro Martinez as he comes towards the end of his contract remains to be seen after another member of United’s leadership team took aim at Wilcox’s recruitment after the defeat by Atletico Madrid. It is said to have caused an angry clash between Martinez and summer signing Tielemans on the way back from Spain.

Martinez looks to be heading for the Old Trafford exit, but it will be interesting to see if the arrival of his compatriot Pochettino – a combative Argentine centre back in much the same mould as a player – has an impact on that.

As a former defender, Pochettino won’t need telling that leaking 15 goals in the last five games simply isn’t good enough. United have now let in 30 in all competitions this season, the most of any club in Europe’s top five leagues apart from Lens.

They have been appalling at the back, conceding in the opening seconds to Atletico, Como and Villa. Had they been able to hold out and prevent late equalisers against Everton and Tottenham, the additional four points would have them 12th in the table rather than in the relegation zone.

A revolving door of makeshift left backs in the absence of Shaw and Dorgu, De Ligt’s belated comeback and Martinez’s needless red card at Chelsea haven’t helped.

Goalkeeper Senne Lammens, so composed last season, looks considerably more shaky behind a leaky and ever-changing back-four, and had arguably his worst game against Villa last weekend.

Pochettino couldn’t ask for a tougher first test than going to Anfield, and knows that United will have to start by being solid at the back.

Aurélien Tchouaméni has left the France squad with a recurrence of the right adductor injury he suffered at the 2026 World Cup. First checks in Madrid found only groin discomfort, so Real Madrid have not ruled out a key starter for the restart of the title race.

Real Madrid are holding off on any verdict over Aurélien Tchouaméni. The midfielder has returned from international duty with a familiar problem in his right adductor. Yet he has not been ruled out of the Celta game at the Santiago Bernabéu.

The picture in Madrid is less clear-cut than France’s decision might suggest. First checks found discomfort in his right groin area, according to Cadena COPE. Radiological and physical tests were set to begin on Thursday.

#1217. Ten-man Betis survive Navalcarnero scare at Santo Domingo as Riquelme wins it in extra time

Real Betis needed a stoppage-time equaliser and extra time to beat Navalcarnero 3-2 in the Copa del Rey round of 128. Manuel Pellegrini's weakened side avoided an upset and now await the second-round draw.

Real Betis came from behind late on to beat Navalcarnero in the Copa del Rey round of 128 on Thursday 12 November. Riquelme settled the tie in extra time at Santo Domingo. Manuel Pellegrini’s side finished with ten men after Aitor Ruibal was sent off.

The venue carried history for the Betis coach. Santo Domingo is where Pellegrini, then in charge of Real Madrid, suffered the 2009 cup defeat known as the ‘Alcorconazo’, El Gol Digital noted. Navalcarnero, founded in 1953, play in Group V of Segunda Federación. The club moved the tie away from its own Municipal Mariano González ground. It chose Santo Domingo, which holds roughly 5,000, to make room for its more than 2,000 members. The club said money was not the only reason.

Riquelme opened the scoring in the fifth minute from a Ruibal assist, and Betis led at half-time. Álvaro Leis equalised in the 49th minute from a free-kick routine set up by Navalcarnero’s coach. Leis then turned provider for K. Vazquez, who put the hosts ahead in the 79th minute.

Marina levelled in stoppage time, with Ruibal credited with the assist. Riquelme’s second goal came in the 96th minute. Diego Llorente went off in extra time after a heavy blow to the head. Isco missed a penalty in the 117th minute. Already booked in the 90+4th minute, Ruibal received a second yellow and a red card in the 118th. Navalcarnero felt they should have had a penalty for a challenge by Pablo Fornals, and the tie was played without VAR, Infobae (EFE) reported.

The figures show how much Betis dominated. They had 73% of the ball, took 29 shots to Navalcarnero’s 12 and won 13 corners to 3. They completed 864 accurate passes. Dani Ceballos earned a 9.2 rating with 3 key passes. On the same night, Levante also needed extra time in the first round, winning 2-1 away to CD Tarancón.

Betis were without several regulars. Valles, Marc Roca, Abde, Parrott, Deossa and four other players were away on international duty. Cucho Hernández was injured. Betis agreed the new date after talks with the RFEF and Navalcarnero, knowing that any players called up by their national teams would miss the match.

The win follows a 2-0 victory over Elche. For Navalcarnero, the defeat ended a run of five matches without loss, including a 3-2 win over Numancia. They host Getafe II in Segunda División RFEF on Sunday 15 November. Betis visit Sevilla in LaLiga on Saturday 21 November.

#1216. Everton give Burnham something to shout about by booking quarter-final spot

David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

What a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

The lack of discipline in their ranks was exposed when Dan Burn scored a late consolation and ended up in a melee with James Tarkowski and Joelinton. But the issues Jaissle, who lamented that “we must improve”, has to correct are for another day: this contest belonged to Everton.

Thierno Barry had provided the finish that secured a trip to Fleetwood in December and what an opportunity it is for Moyes to make Everton semi-finalists in this competition for the first time since 2016. Whether Grealish will have a part to play in it remains to be seen.

Thierno Barry with Everton's third! 🔵 https://t.co/dyb8fKud8N

The last thing Everton needed on a night of such importance was a distraction. Grealish will have a tough job mending relations, particularly with Moyes, but there was a paradox: though he had caused a major issue for 90 minutes he became an irrelevance.

Moyes is impatient to give Evertonians a big day out and his only focus was on crossing this hurdle – for all that Newcastle have had a turbulent start to the campaign, they are dangerous opponents and you wondered in the fraught opening 30 minutes if they might exacerbate the hosts’ woes.

As Jaissle hopped and squirmed on the sidelines, imploring Newcastle forward, chances came and went: Harvey Barnes had a header saved, Fabian Schar tested Jordan Pickford from 30 yards while Vitalii Mykolenko and James Tarkowski made huge goal-saving challenges.

“We should have scored more goals,” Jaissle, who was dressed as if auditioning for the role of The Milk Tray Man, growled. “It [losing] was shocking as the game was not that bad.”

Moyes was infuriated by Everton’s initial inertia, so much so there was a point when the Scot prevented Merlin Röhl, his own full-back, from taking a throw-in until Tarkowski and Jake O’Brien had complied with his gesturing to get 10 yards further forward.

It might have looked old-fashioned but it worked. Suddenly Everton started asking questions, Hayden Hackney almost got on the end of a cross from Mykolenko, and it encouraged the supporters on the vertiginous South Stand to raise their voices and become more involved.

What they needed was a goal to set things alight and in the 34th minute, it arrived. Tyrique George won possession by Newcastle’s corner flag, the ball dropped at Hackney’s feet and he instinctively ushered it on to James Garner, who whipped a right-footed drive beyond Lukáš Horníček.

James Garner puts Everton in front against Newcastle in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 https://t.co/TzponbWyGU

The roar that greeted it was a mix of elation and wonder, relief and desperation. The locals have grown weary of seeing nights with potential end in disappointment but here was the foothold they craved and the opportunity they were ready to seize. Soon the lead would be doubled.

Hackney would score the goal, converting a super Barry cross, but let us acknowledge the fabulous refereeing of Farai Hallam, who waved play on when he might have whistled for a foul on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall. And how Everton took advantage.

Hayden Hackney doubles Everton's advantage! 🔵 https://t.co/VIY0Iln3nI

It must be said the officiating this week has, in the main, been outstanding. Watching a match without the persistent spectre of VAR has been liberating and you can see the referees have felt free to make decisions on instinct.

The whole experience of knowing a contest cannot be re-refereed has been better for all. It will not catch on, sadly, because too many people have gone too far down the road with VAR, but we should embrace the purity of “old school football” while we can.

Evertonians – the Prime Minister included – certainly embraced the buffer of a second goal and the fact Hackney scored it also felt like a throwback: a player who was plucked out of the Championship in the summer and encouraged by Moyes to show he could make the next step up.

He did that and so, too, did Everton, their progress was assured in the 69th minute when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall dashed down the left and crossed for Barry to finish. Moyes puffed out his cheeks as it hit the net. He, more than most, deserved to enjoy this one.

#1215. Jutglà and Swedberg doubles send Celta Vigo through 5-0 at ten-man Salamanca

Celta Vigo were rarely troubled in the Copa del Rey round of 128 on Friday 13 November. Jutglà struck twice before the half-hour mark, and Swedberg added a late double after Salamanca UDS had gone down to ten men.

The Galician side were 3-0 up at the break at Villares de la Reina. They finished with goals from three different players and assists from five team-mates, against a Salamanca side coached by Jorge García.

Jutglà opened the scoring in the 15th minute, converting an assist from Milla. Eight minutes later he struck again, this time set up by Febas, to put Celta firmly in control.

Antañón made it three in the 39th minute from an Arcos assist. The tie was effectively settled before the interval.

Salamanca’s evening grew harder after the restart. Murua was booked in the 54th minute, and Levrand was shown a straight red card in the 61st minute, leaving the hosts a man short for the final half-hour.

Celta’s only caution came when Lago was booked in the 72nd minute. The visitors then took advantage of the extra man late on. Swedberg scored in the 80th minute from an Aspas assist and struck again in the 82nd, with Galán providing the pass.

Opara was also booked for Salamanca in the 89th minute as the hosts saw out the closing stages.

The result echoes the previous meeting between the clubs in this competition. Celta won 7-0 in Salamanca on 3 December 2024.

5 goles para selar o pase á seguinte rolda 🔥#UDSCelta ⋄ #CopaDelRey pic.twitter.com/v5Kqou8U4w

The win is Celta’s first in any competition since their 2-1 victory over Celtic. In between, they drew 0-0 with Real Betis, lost 3-0 to Rayo Vallecano and 2-1 to Union St. Gilloise, and drew 0-0 with Levante.

For Salamanca, the defeat ended a winning run in which they had beaten Gimnástica Segoviana 1-0 and Real Ávila 3-1.

Salamanca return to Segunda División RFEF Group 5 action at home to Albacete II on Wednesday 18 November. Celta face a far tougher assignment in LaLiga, travelling to Real Madrid on Saturday 21 November.

#1214. USMNT players grapple with Mauricio Pochettino's looming exit to Manchester United

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

While no one has officially confirmed that Mauricio Pochettino is departing the United States men's national team for Manchester United after Michael Carrick's sacking, the faces of Sebastian Berhalter and Folarin Balogun said everything that you needed to know at media availability on Thursday ahead of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals match with Haiti. With a spot in the Nations League final at stake in this competition, there's a need to be professional during this, and they stressed that, but it was also hard to hide emotions when the manager under whom they experienced some of their best times as USMNT internationals and an entire World Cup is about to depart.

When asked about what he wanted to see, Balogun was succinct, saying, "If I had a vote, I would like to keep things the way they are."

He continued, saying, "I think things have been working well; we have a clear sense of identity, we have a clear playing style, and whenever you have a top coach, you'd want him to stay, as it's a no-brainer, so I think for us it's no different."

It's hard not to feel for Balogun after he became the story of the World Cup for the wrong reasons, with his red card rescinded before he played against Belgium in the round of 16, where the USMNT suffered a 4-1 loss, crashing out of the tournament. Then things went from bad to worse when his move to Everton was called off due to a change in contract terms, and now he is struggling for playing time at Monaco. While he still plans to leave the French club in January, the national team camp was supposed to be an escape, but instead it has become another uncertain period as Pochettino's days come to an end. Berhalter confirmed that the team hasn't officially heard anything, but that their focus is still on the game at hand.

"We're focused on going against Haiti twice; they're a good team. You saw at the World Cup, they surprised people, so that's our main focus, and I think the group is ready to play these games," Berhalter said.

Date: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 4:30 p.m. ETLocation: Nu Stadium -- Miami, FloridaTV: TBS | Live stream: HBO MaxOdds: Haiti +750; Draw +440; USMNT -350

Berhalter made his national team debut under Pochettino and hasn't looked back, securing 22 caps for the team and making it hard for the Argentine to decide how he should set up the midfield. Because of that, it's hard not to be reflective in uncertain times like these.

"Personally, on the field and off the field, he's done a lot for me, and from day one he's always believed in me. Before I set foot on the field, I think about the way I play and the way that I try to carry myself," Berhalter said. "He just said it doesn't matter what you're doing on the field; these are already the right things. And to be honest, I can't thank him enough, and regardless if he's coach, not the coach and, I say it every time that he's meant so much to me. And he's helped me develop as a player and as a person, and as a player, that's all you can ask for: to have that trust and have that belief in you. And for me, it's easy to go out there and just do my job so, he's meant a good deal to me for sure."

This is all tough to manage while having games to play. Sure, players will say they're going to be professionals, and these are people who have dealt with stress and needed to maintain that professionalism while doing so, but from a human perspective, it's a well-liked coach leaving on short notice. Even if people anticipated that Pochettino might not make it through to the 2030 World Cup and his departure was a sign that a coach who has done well at the helm was leaving, that doesn't make it any easier on the players. If they go ahead quickly against Haiti on Saturday, they could turn the match into a celebration of what has been so great while playing for Pochettino, but going behind can have a cascading impact where doubt starts to creep in. It's something that the USMNT will need to avoid, even if the future is bright for this squad, no matter who is coaching them.

Pochettino helped raise the standard, and with young players like Cavan Sullivan, Adri Mehmeti, Matias Albert, Neil Pierre and Julian Hall, the future is already here, and no one can feel complacent about their spots. These are things that the new coach can bring in, and Pochettino's leadership can set a new standard of what to look for.

"Yeah, I think the benefit and the blessing when you have a great coach is you know the standard," Balogun said. "I think Poch definitely raised the standard since he's been in charge. I think you guys have seen that, just the intensity of training, how we approach games, he's changed our way of thinking as players, from calling the friendlies that we have in certain camps official games, not official games. He wants us to just be of a mindset to go out there and win."

"He's laid the foundation, and I think we, as players, have that ownership to not just do that because Poch was in charge; I think we have the ownership as players to carry that out because we know the standard," he continued. "So yeah, I think that's the benefit of having a top coach, and I'm sure you know whether he's here or not, the US will look to replace him with another top coach."

Who succeeds Pochettino will be important, but what the players have learned from his time will be invaluable, so the standard can't slip from here. As Balogun said, it's time to take ownership of their own future because while the coaches may change, the players tasked with leading this team back to the top of Concacaf are already here and understand the task at hand.
